about: Ten mysteries about real people of the Walled City in the week Mon 15 - Sun 21 Dec 1986, from easy (1) to hard (10). Each case names a real person (data/people.json); data/routines.json puts that person in the answer rooms at the times of "when". Each case has five clues, from weak to strong, and the story that the player gets when the case is solved. Each clue and each quote has its source.

notes.rule_from_john: The LAST clue of each case must be very helpful but must not give the answer outright.
notes.tiers: Cases 1-3 give the street and the hour early. Cases 4-6 give the street; the player works out the hour. Cases 7-8 give only the trade and a quote. Cases 9-10 need two sources together and the peel, or a chain of clues.
notes.answer_types: type "person": the player finds the person (the rooms are where the routine puts the person at the times of "when"). type "room": the player finds the room (case 10); the coordinator can also count a click on the person in it.
notes.found_check: Each answer is in its rooms on 3 or more days of the week, at the times that the clues give. I checked this against data/routines.json: cases 1 and 9 on 6 days, the others on 7 days.
for_the_game: The building panel names the places, for example "Cheng San's ruler factory" or "Ng family flat, Room A, 7/F, 8 Sz Kung St". A player who clicks the right building thus sees the answer. Hide the names of the answer places until the case is solved, or keep them as a reward for a careful search.
Decoy, case 2: data/room_uses.json puts the pigeon lofts at 75:0:0 (G/F of the next building). The book and the routine put the man on roof:59.
Decoy, case 3: data/room_uses.json has a second place for the barber's shop, at 186:0:2 (from the map pin). The routine uses 201:0:0.
Decoy, case 7: the Pak Hop Ruler Factory (百合尺廠, 111:0:2) is also on Tai Chang Street. Its clearance file names no person.
Decoy, case 10: the building labelled 8 Sz Kung Street (173) does not hold the flat.

Case 10: Albert Ng also said "The top floor was the thirteenth floor" (Beijing Visitor). His building in the model (171) has 11 storeys. Building 189 ("near 8 Sz Kung Street") has 13. The clues do not use the thirteenth floor.

cases.title: The rooftop postie

answer.when: Mon-Sat: at the store 09:00-09:40, then on the round until 12:30 (Mon-Fri also 13:15-14:30). All hours are inferred.

cases.brief: Two postmen carry the mail of the whole City. On each working morning, their round starts from a store on Lo Yan Street (老人街) at about 09:00 (an inferred hour). Find the younger postman, Lam Po-chun (林寶鎮).

clues.text: He started on the City round in 1979, when he was 19. In this week of December 1986 he is 26.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: He does not use a map. He learned the pathways from his sifu (teacher), the senior postman Lui Man Sang, who is 12 years older.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: First he sorts the City's mail by hand at the Lung Kong Road (龍崗道) Post Office, outside the City. Thus he is not in the City before about 09:00 (inferred).
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: He wears a cap against the drips and carries the postbag on his back. The locals call him 'hu xu zi' (beardie) for his small moustache.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: The store is on the G/F, at the end of Lo Yan Street near Tung Tau Tsuen Road (東頭村道). Two postmen wait there with the mail: click each of them.
clues.source: the model (data/room_uses.json, data/routines.json)
clues.cite: place A78, Store on Lo Yan Street (basis likely)

cases.solved: You found Lam Po-chun (林寶鎮), 'postman Ah-Po'. He and Mr Lui were the only two postmen with the skills for this maze, and the locals called them 'the rooftop posties'. In a power cut he took out a torch and walked children and old people up to their homes. Once he took a mother and her little boy and girl up to the 12th floor: "afterwards, every time they saw me, they waved to me from the distance and every year they gave me a Christmas card." The two children grew up and became social workers. In 2004 a box came to the Post Office, addressed to 'Postman Ah-Po', with a fabric doll of him inside. "I vividly remember everything about that extraordinary place."

cases.title: Birds over Lo Yan Street

answer.when: every day 14:00-17:00 (the caption gives "mid-afternoon"; the exact hours are inferred); also 06:30-08:00 and 13:30-14:00 (inferred)

cases.brief: Somewhere on Lo Yan Street (老人街), a man keeps racing pigeons on the roof of his apartment building. At one time he had more than 1000 birds. Find him with his pigeons.

clues.text: He lets the birds fly "usually in mid-afternoon when there was a lull in the number of landings at Kai Tak Airport". The model gives 14:00 to 17:00 (inferred).
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: He moved into the City in 1981, when he worked for Hongkong Telecom. He bought his flat for $68,000.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: "I always whistle before I feed them." The whistle calls the young birds back to the loft.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: His cages are on the roof of the building where he lives. He asked the owner of the top flat for leave to build them.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: Watch the roofs at the end of Lo Yan Street near Tung Tau Tsuen Road (東頭村道). His building has 12 storeys, and his own flat is on 2/F.
clues.source: the model (data/room_uses.json, data/routines.json)
clues.cite: place B72, Chan Kwan Leung's flat (basis likely)

cases.solved: You found Chan Kwan Leung (陳昆亮) on his roof, with his birds in the sky above the City. "I enjoyed looking at them and they looked back at me - each of us having quite different thoughts." He quit his job to care for them, and he did not tell his parents or his wife. His birds race home from Xiamen and Shanghai, and often win most of the first ten places. In January 1987 one of his pigeons comes home from Shanghai. "I was so happy, but the same day the Housing Department came to register me as a resident of the Walled City and announced the clearance." On that day he decides to close his pigeon business.

cases.title: The barber's pole
cases.brief: Somewhere on Tai Chang Street (大井街), a barber opens his shop at 9am every day. Find him at work.

clues.text: He bought a flat on Tung Tau Tsuen Road (東頭村道) in 1974. He came into the City every day only after he took over the shop in 1985.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: He and his wife cut hair together. His is the only hair parlour inside the City, and it is cheaper than the barbers outside.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: "We used to open at 9am and close when there were no more customers - it was very flexible." The model closes the shop at about 20:00 (inferred).
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: A barber's pole marks his door, a little down Tai Chang Street from a busy corner store.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: His entrance faces the darkness of Tai Chang Street, not far from the one Government standpipe inside the City. Find the standpipe, then look at the G/F shops near it.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)
clues.cite: p29; the standpipe in the model: data/utilities.json P1

cases.solved: You found Ho Chi Kam (何智錦) at work, scissors in hand. "Running the barber's shop here didn't make me wealthy, but I didn't have to worry about my next meal either." In January 1987 the Government announces the clearance. After it, he works for others again, for 30 per cent of what he earns, and comes here only on Wednesdays, his day off. On 14 January 1987 a resident, 芬姐, heard the news during a perm in a salon inside the City. Ho said that his shop was the only hair parlour inside the City. His shop closed in 1991, shortly before the second phase of the clearance.

cases.title: The map maker

answer.when: at home on every evening and night: Mon-Fri 18:15-19:30 and from 21:30; Sat from 17:30; Sun from 17:00 (all inferred); in the lanes on weekday evenings and at the weekend (inferred)

cases.brief: In this week, an engineering student is drawing a map of the whole City by hand. He lives high up in a building on Tung Tau Tsuen Road (東頭村道), on the edge of the City. Find him.

clues.text: He moved into the City when he married, to start his family in a small home of his own.
clues.source: M+ (Hong Kong), audio guide, 'Kowloon Walled City—aerial view from the southwest' (Ian Lambot, 1989/2013)

clues.text: His work relates to mechanical drawing. He maps "the intertwined streets, and the upper-level walkways connecting different buildings".
clues.source: M+ audio guide 8038 (English), Kowloon Walled City—Aerial View from the Southwest

clues.text: By day he studies outside the City. The map takes him four months, and he finishes it in March 1987: in this week it is about half done. He walks the lanes on weekday evenings and at the weekend (inferred hours).
clues.source: WSJ 2014, People chapter
clues.cite: People chapter (the four months); the finish in March 1987 is in the WSJ narration (primary-sources/wsj-kwc-2014/SOURCE.md)

clues.text: A newspaper fact box (WSJ, 2014) gives his home of 1985-88: Room B, on 12/F.
clues.source: WSJ 2014, People chapter

clues.text: In the model, 12/F is the top floor of his building on Tung Tau Tsuen Road. Peel the City to 12/F late on a weekday evening, after 21:30 (inferred).
clues.source: the model (data/room_uses.json, data/routines.json)
clues.cite: place T4 (basis verified); routine of chan-cheung-chuen

cases.solved: You found Chan Cheung-chuen (陳祥全) at his table, with half a map of the City in front of him. As a boy he came here with classmates: "The dark corners and the intertwined streets were perfect for hide and seek." Here neighbours cook with their windows open and call across the gap: "Hey do you have some soy sauce?" He finishes his map in March 1987, two months after the Government announces the clearance. Later he said that he paid little attention to the clearance, because he was only a tenant (我沒有用心理會清拆，因為我只是個租客). Like you, he walked these lanes to hold the whole City on one sheet of paper.

cases.title: The patrol book

answer.when: every day 05:30-14:00 and 15:30-19:00; all hours are inferred

cases.brief: Police officers walk the main streets of the City two or three times a day. On Kwong Ming Street (光明街), they sign a patrol book outside a fishball shop. Find the young owner at work.

clues.text: As a boy he came from Chiu Chow (潮州) with his parents and his elder brother. The family settled in Lok Fu (樂富), outside the City.
clues.source: HK01 (香港01), 九龍城寨︱德興魚蛋老闆城寨起家躍升行業龍頭　見證山寨工場沒落, 20 Jul 2024

clues.text: In 1983, at 24, he opened his own wholesale shop with HK$6,000. The landlord came from his home area and let the shop cheaply.
clues.source: HK01 (香港01), 九龍城寨︱德興魚蛋老闆城寨起家躍升行業龍頭　見證山寨工場沒落, 20 Jul 2024

clues.text: Kwong Ming Street has several fishball workshops, and also pig-blood, plastic-flower and garment workshops.

clues.text: Today he still wakes at 5am every day to make the fish paste, and he works 364 days a year. The model gives him the same habits in 1986 (inferred).
clues.source: i-Discover Asia, Kowloon City walk, 'Tak Hing Fishballs'

cases.solved: You found 林羅平, whom everyone calls 平哥, at work in his shop. Many people call the City a place without law, but he disagrees: the police sign their patrol book outside his door. Here he needs no licence and pays no tax, and his landlord, a man from his home area, lets the shop cheaply. Of his neighbours he said: 「街坊街里還成天打招呼，好融洽的。」 (they greeted each other all day long). After the clearance he and his elder brother moved the business to Fuk Lo Tsun Road (福佬村道), in Kowloon City (九龍城). In June 2026, at 67, he still worked there 364 days a year, with his wife, May姐. He still uses the machine that he carried out of the City.

cases.title: Before dawn on Lo Yan Street

answer.when: every day 04:00-06:00, 08:15-10:00 and 12:30-14:45 (04:00, the market from 06:15 to 08:00, 09:00, 10:00 and 15:00 are sourced; the other times are inferred)

cases.brief: A roast-meat workshop on Lo Yan Street (老人街) is hot long before dawn. Its owner sells the meat in a market outside the City. Find him in his workshop.

clues.text: He came to Hong Kong in 1978, at 35, from Guangdong, where he was a farmer. From 1971 he tried almost every year to cross the border, and each time they caught him and put him in prison.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: He is an unlicensed hawker in Wong Tai Sin (黃大仙) market. He has been arrested five times.

clues.text: He sells in the market from 6.15am to 8am. Then he comes back for breakfast, and at 9am he starts work again. At about 10am he goes home to cook lunch and rest.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: His workshop is not at street level. In the model it is on 1/F, on Lo Yan Street between the Yamen (衙門) and Lung Chun Road (龍津道). Peel the City to 1/F.
clues.source: the model (data/room_uses.json, data/routines.json)
clues.cite: place B41, Yim Kwok Yuen's cooked-meat workshop (basis likely)

cases.solved: You found Yim Kwok Yuen (嚴國源) at his ovens, in the heat and the smell of roast pork. Of his village he said: "Life was not very different from death in China." Here the work is hard and the ovens are hot, but "as the returns belong to us, it's worthwhile." He married in Canton, and his wife and son wait there for leave to join him. Later he said: "I first applied eight years ago, but I'll be satisfied if they can come before the Walled City is demolished." And: "Coming from such a poor place, I thought Hong Kong was heaven."

cases.title: The ruler maker's night watch

answer.when: almost always: at work 10:00-24:00 and asleep in the factory at night; out for breakfast at about 08:00-09:30 (inferred)

cases.brief: Somewhere in the City, a man makes wooden rulers. He said: "I have to stay here at night otherwise the drug addicts would steal everything." Find him.

clues.text: He was a seaman. At the end of 1967, after all six of his children were born, he came back to Hong Kong, at about 40.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: He saws wood from Borneo by machine. His daughter prints the measurements on the rulers upstairs.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: "Normally I start after 10am and often work until midnight or later. I stop for dinner at 7pm and rest until 9, then start painting."
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: In 1968 he moved his factory into the City, to Tai Chang Street (大井街), because the rent was cheaper and the premises were bigger.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: The model holds two ruler factories on Tai Chang Street. The map in the book marks his factory (no. 8) near the end of the street at Tung Tau Tsuen Road (東頭村道). It is on the G/F.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014), The Map, Anna Dalgliesh
clues.cite: pp352-353, no. 8; the model, place B1 (basis likely); the other factory is in the clearance file HKRS1255-3-262

cases.solved: You found Cheng San (鄭山) among his saws and his paint. "I live here all the time and seldom leave the City - except to go to a nearby restaurant in the morning." Once all his children had supper with him here; now his youngest daughter cooks for him before she goes home. A twelve-inch ruler sells for a little over $30 a dozen. When the clearance comes, he tells the Housing Department (房屋署) officer to get lost. "I don't want the Walled City to be demolished because I could work for a few more years; once it's knocked down, I will have to retire." He made rulers here for 22 years and moved out in 1990.

cases.title: Knocks in the small hours

answer.when: every day 08:00-18:30 and 19:30-23:00 (the opening hours are sourced; the dinner break is inferred)

cases.brief: A herbal doctor said: "Although officially we are open from 8am to 11pm, people always knock on your door in the small hours of the morning asking for this or that medicine." Find him.

clues.text: He came to Hong Kong from Chiu Chow (潮州) county in 1947. He opened his own store in 1955, at the age of 29.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: His father was a herbal doctor and taught him. He sells mainly herbs and also gives consultations; some clients come across from the Island.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: He lives high up, "where I can see the sea and the sights at night". The City faces south to the sea.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)

clues.text: His store is on Lung Chun Road (龍津道). Chinese medicines fill one side of it, and Western toiletries the other.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)
clues.cite: p82 and the caption on p82

clues.text: His building had two storeys, and it was rebuilt as a block of 11 storeys. In the model, that block has a plan number for a label, not a street address. His store is on its G/F.
clues.source: City of Darkness Revisited (Girard and Lambot, 2014)
clues.cite: p82; the model, place A54 (basis likely)

cases.solved: You found Chan Pui Yin (陳沛然), the herbal doctor of Lung Chun Road. "It is a bit like back home in the villages in China - a harmonious state of anarchy." Here a child of five can carry a $500 note to a store for change, and "no one would dream of robbing the kid". He drinks well water and likes its taste. The City once had two big wells, "known as the eyes of one of the nine dragons of Kowloon". One is still in use; a building now stands on the other. His three sons and his daughter grew up here "without using drugs".

answer.when: Mon-Sat 10:00-13:00 and 14:00-19:00 (Tue, Thu and Sat from 15:30); Sun 11:00-16:00. All hours are inferred.

cases.brief: A man said that his property business became the biggest in the Walled City. The book that quotes him gives no address. Find him at his desk.

clues.text: He was born in 1951 and grew up in the City. At about 13 he delivered drinks to the opium dens, the gambling dens and the sex shows.

cases.solved: You found Chu Yiu Shan (朱耀山) at the desk of his company, 恒暉地產. People leave their flats with him, and he sells them on their behalf when the price is fair. He said: "As a resident who had lived in the City for many years, I was in a good position to find out who the real owners were." The water men helped him: "I knew the people who 'released' the water, and they helped me identify who had built which properties." When the Government announces the clearance in January 1987, he moves to Junk Bay. Later he said: "The demolition of the Walled City will be the end of everything. I only hope that I can get a hawker's licence."

cases.title: The eighth floor

answer.when: the room is there at any hour; Albert is at home on most evenings and every night (inferred)

cases.brief: A newspaper wrote of a boy who "went to school outside the Walled City but remembers playing on its rooftop and in its corridors". Find the room where his family lives.

clues.text: The boy is Albert Ng Kam-po (吳錦波), from a Chiu Chow (潮州) family. His family moved in in 1975, for "the relatively cheaper price".
clues.source: Asia Society Hong Kong, 'Life in Kowloon Walled City' (2013 roundtable page)

clues.text: For him "the roof top was the only place to play". When a ball fell, "we had to run from the eight floor all the way to the third floor and get the ball back."
clues.source: Beijing Visitor, 'Journey into the Soul of the Kowloon Walled City with Pastor Albert Ng'

clues.text: "I lived on the eighth floor and there was no elevator." In Hong Kong the ground floor is G/F, and the floor above it is 1/F. Thus his "eighth floor" is 7/F.
clues.source: Beijing Visitor, 'Journey into the Soul of the Kowloon Walled City with Pastor Albert Ng'

clues.text: "Every single day, we would have to go the public water stations so we could drink and shower." In the model he fetches water at the standpipe in the late afternoon (inferred). Follow him home.
clues.source: Beijing Visitor, 'Journey into the Soul of the Kowloon Walled City with Pastor Albert Ng'

clues.text: A newspaper fact box gives the flat as Room A, 7/F, 8 Sz Kung St. (社公街). But the numbers in the City moved all the time. In the model, the flat is not in the building labelled 8 Sz Kung Street: peel the City to 7/F and try its neighbours.
clues.source: WSJ 2014, People chapter
clues.cite: People chapter, fact box; City of Darkness Revisited p146 (the numbers); the model, place T1 (basis verified)

cases.solved: You found the home of Albert Ng Kam-po (吳錦波): Room A, 7/F, the eighth storey of its building. "I used to live in a one bedroom flat and it used to be about 200 square feet." Five people live here, and the one bedroom is for his mother and his younger sister. "The wall was always wet and mouldy and it used to smell really, really bad." In 1988 he leaves for the University of Hong Kong (香港大學), and later he becomes a pastor. Of the hard years here he said: "But we had hope".
